failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Agents returned a salient associated item or placeholder rather than the target requested by the clue, despite existing target and wordplay guidance.

rejected_edits.content: For passive renaming clues such as “they were once called X,” resolve the pronoun to the thing being renamed and answer that thing's conventional identity; do not answer its inventor or namer unless the clue asks who.
rejected_edits.target: Before choosing a candidate, use the clue's head nouns and pronouns to identify the kind of answer requested: a manner, place, role, institution, species, person, or other category. Return that target, not a consequence, associated entity, or example used to identify it.

rejected_edits.content: When choosing a name form, distinguish genuinely generic labels from words that form part of the entity's conventional proper name. Retain conventional initials and lexicalized type words in established names; omit an entity or location type label only if it is not part of the conventional name and the shorter form is accepted and unambiguous.
rejected_edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.

rejected_edits.content: For a prompt consisting only of a person's name, infer an omitted relation from context only when one relation is clearly foregrounded—for example, when context consistently identifies an officeholder with a particular jurisdiction. Answer that relation rather than merely repeating the person's title or office. If several relations are equally plausible, do not guess.
